key_insight: Among four WC-10Co-4Cr thermal-sprayed coatings, HVAF delivered the best overall balance of wear and corrosion resistance, while HVOF was a close second for wear performance.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that spray process selection strongly controls coating density, hardness, friction, wear, and corrosion behavior for stainless-steel protection in demanding tribological environments.
method: Prepared WC-10Co-4Cr coatings on 304 stainless steel using APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF.
Compared microstructure, Vickers hardness, wear rate/friction, and electrochemical corrosion performance.
Evaluated wear scars to identify dominant mechanisms and coating failure features.
evidence_signal: Compared with bare 304 stainless steel, the coatings had much higher hardness and far lower wear rates, and HVAF achieved the best corrosion metrics with the lowest corrosion current density and highest corrosion resistance.
watch_item: Performance differences are process- and condition-dependent, so these results should be validated for the specific service load, environment, and coating thickness/porosity required in deployment.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
